question: Why is the protein-digesting enzyme pepsin first released in an inactive form called pepsinogen?

options.A: To ensure it only activates when it mixes with bile in the large intestine
options.B: To help the stomach absorb large amounts of water before digestion starts
options.C: To prevent the enzyme from digesting the protein structures of the cells that produce it
options.D: To allow it to travel safely through the bloodstream without breaking down fats

explanation: It's a smart safety feature! If stomach cells made active pepsin right away, the enzyme would turn around and digest the very cells that created it.

question: What is the main reason nurses encourage patients with fevers to drink plenty of fluids?

options.A: To force the kidneys to shut down and rest overnight
options.B: To dilute the red blood cells and prevent clotting
options.C: To replace fluid lost through sweating and increased metabolism
options.D: To lower the body temperature instantly from the inside

explanation: Correct! Sweating from a fever and breathing faster both drain water from your body, so drinking up keeps dehydration away.

question: Which data collection method involves a researcher joining a group setting to watch daily routines naturally?

options.A: Participant observation
options.B: Closed-ended numeric survey
options.C: Biochemical laboratory assay
options.D: Automated blood pressure reading

explanation: Correct! By joining in or quietly watching the natural environment, the researcher gets a real-world view of daily behaviors.

question: What is the primary goal of family planning when it comes to maternal health?

options.A: To replace the need for routine antenatal checkups
options.B: To increase the total birth rate in rural areas
options.C: To space pregnancies and prevent high-risk births
options.D: To completely eradicate all infectious diseases

explanation: Spot on! Family planning gives women control over their pregnancies, helping them avoid very young or older high-risk ages and keeping healthy gaps between kids.

question: How does soluble fiber help manage blood sugar levels in diabetes?

options.A: It replaces the need for daily oral diabetes medications.
options.B: It slows down glucose absorption in the digestive tract.
options.C: It destroys excess insulin circulating in the bloodstream.
options.D: It turns directly into stored energy in the liver.

explanation: Soluble fiber forms a gel during digestion that delays sugar entering the bloodstream, preventing sharp spikes. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h5)

question: What is the main job of the mucociliary escalator in our airways?

options.A: Exchanging oxygen and carbon dioxide in the tiny air sacs
options.B: Making surfactant to keep the lungs from collapsing
options.C: Filtering big dust bits right inside the nose
options.D: Sweeping trapped dirt and mucus upward toward the throat

explanation: Think of the mucociliary escalator like a tiny conveyor belt in your respiratory tract. It uses beating hair-like cilia and mucus to push dust and germs up to your throat so you can swallow or cough them out cleanly!

question: During which phase of cancer development do cells gain aggressive traits and learn to spread?

options.A: Progression
options.B: Initiation
options.C: Promotion
options.D: Encapsulation

explanation: Progression is the final, full-speed-ahead phase where the cells become truly malignant and start invading.

question: Which cranial nerves have their roots located right inside the brain stem?

options.A: Cranial nerves III through XII
options.B: Only the spinal accessory nerve
options.C: All twelve pairs of cranial nerves
options.D: Cranial nerves I and II only

explanation: Ten out of the twelve pairs of cranial nerves (from number three to twelve) actually originate right inside the brain stem. Neat, right?

question: Why is picking the right research design so important for your everyday patient care?

options.A: It guarantees that every patient will recover quickly
options.B: It stops nurses from having to read previous literature
options.C: It ensures findings are valid and useful for patient care
options.D: It eliminates the need for any statistical data analysis

explanation: You got it! A solid design cuts down errors so the evidence we find is safe and reliable enough to use right at the bedside.

question: When the Renin-Angiotensin-Aldosterone System (RAAS) kicks in, what is its main job?

options.A: Increase blood volume and cause vasoconstriction
options.B: Decrease heart rate and promote fluid excretion
options.C: Stimulate direct potassium loss through the sweat glands
options.D: Dilate peripheral arteries and lower blood pressure

explanation: When blood pressure drops too low, RAAS comes to the rescue by tightening blood vessels and telling the kidneys to hold onto water and salt to boost pressure back up.

question: What are the two big features that define all stem cells?

options.A: Programmed death and shrinkage
options.B: Rapid mutation and anaplasia
options.C: Self-renewal and potency
options.D: Encapsulation and metastasis

explanation: Spot on! Stem cells are amazing because they can both make copies of themselves (self-renewal) and turn into specialized cells (potency).

question: During which weeks of pregnancy do the baby's main body organs actively form?

options.A: Weeks 10 to 14
options.B: Weeks 32 to 36
options.C: Weeks 3 to 8
options.D: Weeks 20 to 24

explanation: Brilliant! Weeks 3 to 8 are known as the embryonic period, when all the primary organ systems are shaped and laid down. Keep up the great momentum!

question: What exactly are 'Pick bodies' seen under a microscope in brain tissue?

options.A: Scars from previous traumatic head injuries
options.B: Deposits of calcium in the brain blood vessels
options.C: Clumps of abnormal tau protein inside nerve cells
options.D: Infections caused by bacteria in the spinal fluid

explanation: Pick bodies are just microscopic clumps of tangled tau protein. When neurons get weighed down by these clumps, they start to struggle and break down.

question: Which main nerve links the gastrointestinal tract directly to the brain?

options.A: The phrenic nerve
options.B: The trigeminal nerve
options.C: The vagus nerve
options.D: The sciatic nerve

explanation: Spot on! The vagus nerve is the primary communication highway connecting your gut and your brain.

question: What is the main physical sign you will see in an adult with acromegaly?

options.A: Enlargement of the hands, feet, and facial bones
options.B: Sudden and severe hair loss all over the scalp
options.C: Extreme weight loss with rapid muscle wasting
options.D: Sudden, very rapid growth in height during childhood

explanation: In adults, bone growth plates are already closed, so excess growth hormone can't make them taller. Instead, bones and soft tissues grow outward and thicken—giving broader hands, feet, and facial features.

question: Why is it important to share evaluation results back with the community members?

options.A: It proves to them that health workers are superior planners
options.B: It eliminates the need for any future community meetings
options.C: It forces them to pay taxes for the healthcare they received
options.D: It maintains motivation and highlights areas for improvement

explanation: Brilliant! Giving feedback lets the community see the impact of their hard work, keeps them excited, and guides what needs fixing next.

question: A nurse gets lower back pain after lifting heavy patients without help. What type of hazard is this?

options.A: Chemical hazard
options.B: Ergonomic hazard
options.C: Physical hazard
options.D: Biological hazard

explanation: Lifting heavy loads with poor body mechanics strains the muscles and joints, making it a classic ergonomic issue. Always remember your proper lifting posture!

question: What is the main job of the testes in the male body?

options.A: Producing lubricating fluids for intercourse
options.B: Producing sperm and testosterone
options.C: Storing urine from the bladder
options.D: Regulating core body temperature directly

explanation: The testes are the male reproductive glands responsible for making sperm and the hormone testosterone.

question: When should a mother have her very first postnatal checkup after giving birth in a facility?

options.A: Only when the baby falls sick
options.B: When the child is ready for school
options.C: Within 24 hours of birth
options.D: At the end of the sixth week

explanation: Correct! The first 24 hours carry the highest risk for bleeding and newborn issues, so early checks are vital.

question: When food prices shoot up due to inflation, how do many families change what they eat?

options.A: They grow all their missing food requirements in backyard container gardens
options.B: They substitute nutrient-dense foods with cheaper, calorie-dense refined carbohydrates
options.C: They automatically increase their daily intake of fresh fruits and lean meats
options.D: They stop eating entirely until government food subsidies arrive in the mail

explanation: When money gets tight, families swap out expensive veggies and proteins for cheaper filler foods that fill the belly but lack vitamins.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to healthcare access in Nigerian communities?

options.A: Gender inequality limiting women's health choices
options.B: Poverty and inability to pay for medications
options.C: An oversupply of free universal healthcare facilities in every village
options.D: Stigma and discrimination against stigmatized health conditions

explanation: Spot on! Having too many free clinics is definitely not our problem—scarcity, poverty, and cost are the real barriers.

question: A patient has an infected open leg fracture that hasn't healed over the past eight months, despite short courses of oral antibiotics. What type of osteomyelitis is this?

options.A: Aseptic bone infarction
options.B: Transient bone bruising
options.C: Acute hematogenous osteomyelitis
options.D: Chronic osteomyelitis

explanation: When an infection sticks around for many months and fights off standard treatments, it has turned into chronic osteomyelitis.

question: Why do nurses use the idea of a 'standard drink' instead of just counting glasses or bottles?

options.A: Serving sizes and alcohol strengths vary widely between different beverages
options.B: It makes tax calculations easier for local health authorities
options.C: Spirits contain no pure alcohol when mixed with water
options.D: Bottles of wine always contain exactly one standard serving

explanation: Not all drinks are poured equal! A big mug of stout packs way more punch than a small glass of wine. Using standard drinks helps patients track their real intake accurately.

question: Where do most traditional drug administration abbreviations come from?

options.A: Ancient Greek literature
options.B: Latin terminology
options.C: Modern medical shorthand
options.D: French pharmaceutical guides

explanation: Great job! Most medical abbreviations are rooted in old Latin terms that doctors and pharmacists used historically to describe how drugs should be taken.

question: Why do diagnostic tools in primary health care need to be simple and affordable?

options.A: Laboratory tests are always completely inaccurate
options.B: Primary care centers have limited resources and high community needs
options.C: Nurses are not allowed to use expensive equipment
options.D: Patients in rural communities rarely get sick

explanation: Primary health care serves everyday people with tight budgets, so we need accessible and cost-effective tools that work well in our local clinics. Great job thinking practically!

question: Which learning domain do standard multiple-choice exams primarily test?

options.A: Kinesthetic domain
options.B: Psychomotor domain
options.C: Affective domain
options.D: Cognitive domain

explanation: Written tests focus on mental skills, recall, and how you process information—all part of the cognitive domain. You use this brainpower every day in class!

question: How many links make up the standard chain of infection?

options.A: Ten links
options.B: Six links
options.C: Four links
options.D: Eight links

explanation: You've got this! The chain of infection is made up of six links, starting from the infectious agent all the way to the susceptible host.

question: Why do we actually study nursing theories in school? What is their main job?

options.A: To dictate how much medication a patient should receive
options.B: To eliminate the need for doctor and nurse collaboration
options.C: To guide clinical practice and provide a scientific base
options.D: To replace hospital policies and procedure manuals

explanation: Think of nursing theories as the bedrock of our profession! They give us a clear, scientific reason for the way we care for patients every single day.

question: What does a hysterosalpingography (HSG) procedure mainly check in a female patient?

options.A: Whether the fallopian tubes are open
options.B: Levels of progesterone during ovulation
options.C: The thickness of the uterine lining
options.D: The total number of remaining eggs

explanation: An HSG uses a special dye and X-rays to check if the fallopian tubes are clear or blocked. Simple and clear!

question: What is the main goal of patient safety in healthcare?

options.A: To eliminate the cost of hospital stays
options.B: To ensure doctors make all clinical choices
options.C: To speed up the hospital discharge process
options.D: To prevent accidental harm to patients

explanation: Patient safety is all about keeping patients protected from accidental injury or harm while they are receiving care from us. You've got this!

question: What is the primary purpose of hospital bed accessories?

options.A: To increase the speed of patient discharge
options.B: To improve patient care, safety, and outcomes
options.C: To replace the need for daily bed baths
options.D: To reduce the cost of hospital linen

explanation: These specialized devices are designed primarily to support therapeutic care, comfort, and patient safety while in bed. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h1)

question: Which protective layer of the meninges wraps directly and tightly around the surface of the spinal cord?

options.A: Pia mater
options.B: Arachnoid mater
options.C: Periosteum
options.D: Dura mater

explanation: Great job! The pia mater is the innermost, delicate layer that hugs every single curve and groove of the spinal cord and brain like a second skin.

question: How do family planning 'supply methods' differ mainly from long-acting methods like coils or implants?

options.A: They can only be obtained through a surgical procedure
options.B: They provide permanent sterilization after a single use
options.C: They are inserted by a doctor and last for five years
options.D: They require active user action during or before every sexual act

explanation: Supply methods rely entirely on you remembering to use them correctly each time, unlike implants or coils that work continuously in the background. You've got this!

question: Why are engineering controls generally preferred over personal protective equipment?

options.A: They do not rely on the worker remembering to wear them correctly every day
options.B: They completely eliminate the hazard from the universe
options.C: They are the only legal requirement for hospitals
options.D: They cost nothing to install and maintain over time

explanation: Engineering controls work automatically in the background, reducing human error in safety maintenance. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h4)

question: What does the basal metabolic rate measure?

options.A: Total calories burned during heavy physical exercise
options.B: Extra calories burned due to cold weather exposure
options.C: Energy used specifically to digest a large meal
options.D: Minimum calories needed for basic life functions at rest

explanation: BMR is the baseline energy required by the body to sustain vital organs while completely at rest. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T008#GNS227_U4_T008_h2)

question: Which family planning method protects against both pregnancy AND sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?

options.A: Hormonal implants
options.B: Copper intrauterine devices
options.C: Barrier methods
options.D: Natural fertility awareness

explanation: Great job! Barrier methods like male and female condoms block physical contact and fluids, giving you dual protection against both STIs and unwanted pregnancy.

question: What problem is a varicocele repair surgery designed to fix in men?

options.A: Infection in the prostate gland
options.B: A hormonal imbalance in the pituitary gland
options.C: Enlarged veins in the scrotum that warm the testes
options.D: A complete lack of sperm production in the bone marrow

explanation: Varicoceles trap heat in the scrotum, which hurts sperm. Repairing them cools things down and helps sperm grow healthy again!

question: Why do STI infections in the male urethra often lead to swelling and pus?

options.A: The body produces extra oil to protect the skin from dryness
options.B: White blood cells rush to the invasion site to fight the microbes
options.C: Urine mixes with blood cells to create a protective barrier
options.D: Microbes block normal urine flow and cause back pressure

explanation: Think of white blood cells as your body's emergency responders. When germs attack, they flood the area to fight back, creating that pus we see in infections.

question: How should a nurse balance checking a patient's naked skin for injuries while keeping them warm during step 'E'?

options.A: Avoid taking off any clothes at all to keep them warm
options.B: Turn off all room fans to heat up the room
options.C: Leave the patient completely naked for hours to watch their skin
options.D: Uncover body parts briefly to check them, then cover the patient with warm blankets

explanation: You got it! Quick, targeted checks followed by covering them right back up lets you spot injuries without freezing the patient.

question: Why do nurses play such a big role in carrying out the Essential Drug Programme?

options.A: They work exclusively inside administrative pharmacy offices
options.B: They control the international import budgets for pharmaceuticals
options.C: They interact with patients daily and manage bedside drug use
options.D: They are legally licensed to manufacture commercial vaccines

explanation: Spot on! As a nurse, you are right on the frontline—giving medications, tracking supplies, and teaching patients every single day.

question: A patient with a hairy chest is being hooked up to a telemetry monitor, but the screen shows heavy static. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Replace the entire monitor box with a new unit
options.B: Switch the patient immediately to a 12-lead machine
options.C: Clip the chest hair and prep the skin before placing new electrodes
options.D: Increase the alarm volume so the nursing station can hear it better

explanation: Hair prevents good contact between the electrode and the skin, which causes static and artifact on the screen. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h3)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic with a BP of 220/130 mmHg, chest pain, and confusion. What are they likely experiencing?

options.A: Normal white coat syndrome
options.B: Isolated systolic hypertension
options.C: Hypertensive urgency
options.D: Hypertensive emergency

explanation: Extremely high blood pressure plus signs of brain or heart distress (like confusion and chest pain) makes this a critical medical emergency. You're crushing these clinical scenarios!

question: What is a major source of crystalline silica dust exposure for workers in many Nigerian local communities?

options.A: Operating commercial transport buses in traffic
options.B: Fishing in coastal rivers and marine lagoons
options.C: Artisanal gold mining and stone quarrying
options.D: Weaving traditional cotton fabrics by hand

explanation: Unregulated mining and quarrying activities frequently expose local Nigerian workers to high levels of dangerous silica dust. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T8#GNS213_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which of these is a realistic, patient-centered nutrition goal?

options.A: Walking for twenty minutes after lunch four days a week
options.B: Losing twenty kilograms by the end of this month
options.C: Eating a much healthier diet starting immediately
options.D: Eliminating all food cravings within forty-eight hours

explanation: Brilliant! This goal is specific, achievable, and easy to measure. Small, steady steps lead to big wins.

question: A nursing mother says she cannot afford expensive baby formula or imported supplements. As a nurse, what is your best response?

options.A: Explain that homemade food has no nutritional value for babies
options.B: Show her how to enrich local family staples with mashed beans and green leaves
options.C: Advise her to wait until the child is five years old to eat solid food
options.D: Tell her to stop breastfeeding immediately and buy cow milk instead

explanation: Wonderful nursing care! Always encourage affordable, locally available foods that families can easily prepare and sustain.

question: During a physical assessment, a nurse notices a patient has extremely dry, brittle hair and pale inner eyelids. What should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Normal age-related skin changes
options.B: An overdose of vitamin supplements
options.C: An acute allergic reaction to soap
options.D: Possible nutritional deficiencies

explanation: Physical signs like dry hair and pale mucous membranes often point toward underlying nutritional issues such as lack of protein or iron. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h6)

question: Why does a Quality Assurance Committee need members from different departments (multidisciplinary)?

options.A: To make committee meetings last longer
options.B: To reduce the number of doctors needed in the wards
options.C: Because government laws forbid single-profession committees
options.D: Because patient care involves many different health professionals working together

explanation: Spot on! Since nursing, pharmacy, and medicine all work together for the patient, everyone needs a voice on the team.

question: Why do doctors often use laparoscopy to look closely at the fallopian tubes?

options.A: It requires no anesthesia and is done at the bedside
options.B: It completely cures all tubal blockages
options.C: It uses high-frequency sound waves to measure organ density
options.D: It lets the surgeon see the pelvic organs directly with a camera

explanation: A laparoscope is a tiny lighted camera that gives the surgeon a clear, direct view of what is going on inside the pelvis. You're mastering this topic!

question: How does the World Health Organization (WHO) officially define health?

options.A: The total absence of any infection or physical pain
options.B: The ability to work and function normally in society
options.C: A balance between spiritual and biological body forces
options.D: A state of complete physical, mental, and social well-being

explanation: You've got this! The WHO looks at the whole person. Health isn't just about a strong body; it includes how we feel mentally and how we relate to others around us.

question: A patient has an injury damaging the nerve fibers in their ventral root. What would you expect to see?

options.A: Inability to move the target muscle effector
options.B: Inability of receptors to detect hot temperatures
options.C: Loss of sensation to pinprick in the skin
options.D: Total loss of conscious thought and memory

explanation: Since the ventral root carries the outgoing 'action' command to muscles, damaging it blocks that final signal, leading to weakness or trouble moving.

question: Why is community outreach such an important part of psychiatric nursing?

options.A: It allows nurses to avoid working inside hospitals entirely
options.B: It brings mental health resources directly to vulnerable populations who may not seek care
options.C: It replaces the need for individual counseling sessions
options.D: It guarantees that no one in the community will ever feel sad

explanation: Not everyone can walk into a hospital for help. Outreach bridges the gap and brings care straight to the people who need it most.

question: What do we mean by the term 'hidden hunger'?

options.A: People hide their food insecurity out of shame in rural communities
options.B: Individuals consume adequate calories but lack essential vitamins and minerals
options.C: Food items lose their nutrients completely during traditional cooking
options.D: Laboratory tests cannot detect nutritional shortages in the early stages

explanation: Spot on! 'Hidden hunger' happens when someone gets enough food to feel full (calories), but their body is starving for vital vitamins and minerals. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h1)

question: What does follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) do in the ovaries?

options.A: It helps immature eggs inside the ovaries grow.
options.B: It causes the muscular wall of the uterus to contract strongly.
options.C: It immediately stops all blood flow to the endometrium.
options.D: It thickens the outer layer of the vaginal walls.

explanation: True to its name, FSH 'stimulates' the little follicles in the ovary so the eggs inside can grow and get ready for action.

question: Why do heavy blocks of text usually fail in community health education programs?

options.A: People prefer listening to long audio recordings instead.
options.B: Ink tends to smudge when paragraphs are printed too close together.
options.C: Medical authorities forbid the use of written sentences on posters.
options.D: Low literacy rates in the target population make reading difficult.

explanation: Many community members have limited reading skills. If your poster is packed with heavy text, the main health message gets lost.

question: When public health nurses talk about 'community structure', what are they mostly looking at?

options.A: The financial budget of the local government
options.B: How people are organized and how power is distributed
options.C: The physical blueprint of houses in a neighborhood
options.D: The exact number of hospital beds in a local clinic

explanation: Think of community structure as the backbone of the neighborhood: who holds influence, how groups connect, and how leadership works. Spotting this helps you know who to talk to when you want to start a health project!

question: What important step is needed right after using ethylene oxide gas on medical items?

options.A: Immediate rinsing in sterile water and drying
options.B: Submersion in a neutralizing acid bath
options.C: Exposure to ultraviolet light rays
options.D: Thorough aeration to remove toxic gas residues

explanation: Ethylene oxide gas is toxic to human tissue, so items must air out thoroughly in a special cabinet before anyone touches them.

question: Which type of FGM involves narrowing the vaginal opening and creating a seal?

options.A: Type III
options.B: Type IV
options.C: Type II
options.D: Type I

explanation: Great job! Type III is also called infibulation. It involves cutting and repositioning the labia to form a restrictive seal over the vagina.

question: Which muscle group makes up the main bulk of the pelvic floor?

options.A: Levator ani
options.B: Piriformis
options.C: Obturator internus
options.D: Gluteus maximus

explanation: You nailed it! The levator ani is the star player here—it forms the major muscular sling of the pelvis.

question: How does the DRF system help protect patients from fake or substandard drugs?

options.A: By testing every single pill in a laboratory before selling it
options.B: By destroying all imported medications immediately
options.C: By purchasing drugs only from verified and approved suppliers
options.D: By allowing patients to bring their own drugs from home

explanation: Safety first! By sticking to trusted, approved suppliers, the pharmacy keeps fake medications far away from our patients.

question: Once an expectorant thins out the respiratory mucus, what helps sweep it up toward the throat?

options.A: They absorb the excess fluid so the lungs stay completely dry
options.B: They dissolve the chemical bonds holding the phlegm together
options.C: They sweep the loosened mucus upward toward the throat
options.D: They produce more thick mucus to trap remaining dust particles

explanation: Meet the cilia—tiny hair-like structures in your airways that wave together like a stadium crowd to push that loosened mucus right up and out!

question: Which statement best captures the dimensional approach to mental health?

options.A: It measures symptom severity along a continuous spectrum
options.B: It ignores mild symptoms in favor of severe crises
options.C: It assigns every patient a rigid, permanent label
options.D: It relies solely on blood tests and imaging results

explanation: Instead of a simple yes-or-no box, the dimensional approach looks at how mild, moderate, or severe a client's symptoms are.

question: What emotional heavy lifting comes with an adult child taking care of an aging parent (role reversal)?

options.A: Complete freedom from everyday responsibilities
options.B: Instant wealth and total relaxation
options.C: Confusion, guilt, and emotional tiredness
options.D: Super-human physical strength and endless energy

explanation: It's tough becoming the parent to your own parent. The sudden shift in roles frequently leads to heavy guilt, confusion, and caregiver burnout.

question: What is selective reporting in research?

options.A: Using pseudonyms to protect the identity of study participants
options.B: Aligning numbers by their decimal points in a table
options.C: Highlighting only supportive data while hiding contradictory results
options.D: Choosing between a bar chart and a statistical table

explanation: Selective reporting is an unethical practice where researchers suppress unfavorable findings to present a biased picture. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T4#GNS224_U2_T4_h6)

question: How do the speaker and screen on an AED help you during an emergency?

options.A: They record the conversation between family members and healthcare providers.
options.B: They give clear step-by-step directions to guide the rescuer through the rescue.
options.C: They display the patient's exact medical history and home medications.
options.D: They automatically contact the nearest police station for assistance.

explanation: Even if you are nervous, the AED talks you right through it. Just turn it on and listen to the voice prompts!

question: What is a great way for a father to support the mother after childbirth?

options.A: Isolating the newborn from all family members
options.B: Taking over exclusive breastfeeding duties from the mother
options.C: Assisting with household chores to help the mother rest
options.D: Refusing to allow visitors into the family compound

explanation: New mothers need plenty of physical rest to recover, so a partner stepping in with chores is a huge help!

question: What is the biggest danger of constant, severe scratching when a patient has a skin rash?

options.A: Triggering sudden total hair loss across the entire scalp
options.B: Permanently altering the chemical balance of natural sweat glands
options.C: Breaking the skin barrier through scratching and introducing bacterial infections
options.D: Causing the patient's blood pressure to drop rapidly into shock

explanation: Spot on! Scratching breaks open the skin's protective shield, inviting bacteria to sneak in and cause a secondary infection.

question: What is the main reason healthcare professionals use manuals like the DSM-5?

options.A: To provide clear, standard criteria for diagnosing mental disorders
options.B: To dictate the architectural design of hospital wards
options.C: To replace the need to talk directly with patients
options.D: To calculate the exact financial cost of long-term stays

explanation: Diagnostic manuals give clinicians a shared language and symptom checklist. This helps healthcare teams around the world diagnose and discuss mental health conditions accurately.

question: Why do people stopping heavy alcohol use often experience dangerous symptoms like shaking (tremors) and seizures?

options.A: The brain experiences a rebound effect of hyperexcitability
options.B: The liver fails to filter out toxins quickly enough
options.C: The stomach lining becomes irritated by lack of nutrients
options.D: The muscles lose all stored protein and water

explanation: Brilliant! Since alcohol depresses the brain, taking it away suddenly causes the nervous system to bounce back hard and become dangerously overactive.

question: Why should a nurse check the formulary before giving a drug to a patient?

options.A: To find out which commercial brand name is the most expensive
options.B: To calculate the daily profit margin of the hospital pharmacy department
options.C: To verify normal dosage ranges and check for potential adverse reactions
options.D: To order new stock supplies directly from foreign manufacturers

explanation: Checking first is a great habit! It helps you confirm the safe dose and watch out for side effects before administration.

question: What is the main danger of failing to do regular reassessments in emergency care?

options.A: Doctors will forget to write discharge prescriptions
options.B: The patient will complain about hospital food quality
options.C: Subtle signs of clinical deterioration may be missed until it is too late
options.D: Insurance companies will refuse to pay the hospital bill

explanation: Regular checks help you catch failing vital signs early, giving you time to step in before things take a turn for the worse.

question: A patient undergoing chemotherapy has a very weak immune system. As a nurse, what is your top priority for them?

options.A: Administering live vaccines to boost their active immunity
options.B: Encouraging immediate exposure to crowded public areas
options.C: Stopping all routine vital sign checks to avoid fatigue
options.D: Strict adherence to infection control and hand hygiene

explanation: Because their defenses are down, immunocompromised patients cannot fight off germs easily. Rigorous hand hygiene and infection prevention are true lifesavers here!

question: Why should patients take artemether-lumefantrine tablets with fatty food?

options.A: Fat neutralizes the bitter taste of the crushed tablets
options.B: Fat coats the stomach to completely prevent any nausea
options.C: Fat helps the kidneys excrete the drug much faster
options.D: Fat significantly improves the absorption of the lumefantrine component

explanation: Wonderful! Lumefantrine dissolves best in fat, so a fatty meal helps the body absorb it properly to knock out the malaria.

question: Which part of a homeostatic control system detects a change or stimulus in the environment?

options.A: Receptor
options.B: Control center
options.C: Set point
options.D: Effector

explanation: Receptors act as sensors that pick up changes in the environment and forward that data to the control center. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T10#GNS111_U1_T10_h2)

question: A nurse scores low in medication safety during a review. What should the manager do next?

options.A: Establish a clear plan with check-ins to monitor medication practice improvement
options.B: Ignore the score since annual reviews do not impact daily clinical work
options.C: Reassign the nurse permanently to administrative duties without notice
options.D: Report the nurse directly to the national licensing board immediately

explanation: Good leaders don't just point out mistakes and walk away. They set up a supportive plan with regular check-ins to help you build your confidence and safety.

question: Why do accidental drug overdoses happen so often in young children?

options.A: Children lack the enzymes needed to digest capsules
options.B: Children often mistake colorful pills for candy
options.C: Children have faster metabolisms than adults do
options.D: Children excrete medications much slower through kidneys

explanation: Curious toddlers love to explore! They frequently mistake bright, attractive pills lying around for sweets, which is why safe storage at home is so crucial.

question: Which of these is a classic, everyday cause of conductive hearing loss?

options.A: Presbycusis
options.B: Noise-induced hair cell damage
options.C: Cerumen impaction
options.D: Acoustic neuroma

explanation: Cerumen is just the medical term for earwax! When too much wax builds up and blocks the ear canal, sound waves can't reach the eardrum. A simple cleanup usually fixes it right up.

question: Why does the CSSD follow a strict one-way workflow?

options.A: To make it easier for staff to walk around the department
options.B: To ensure sterilizers are close to the main entrance
options.C: To prevent clean items from crossing paths with dirty items
options.D: To reduce the electricity consumed by heavy machinery

explanation: A one-way flow makes sure that freshly cleaned and sterilized supplies never bump into or cross paths with dirty instruments. Safety first!

question: When can a patient safely start a new method of contraception after a medical abortion?

options.A: Only after waiting six full months
options.B: After the next normal menstrual period
options.C: Immediately on the same day
options.D: Strictly after a surgical checkup

explanation: Correct! Fertility can return almost immediately, so patients can start new birth control methods like pills or implants on the exact same day they take the abortion medications.

question: Which drug class must patients NEVER mix with erectile dysfunction medications like sildenafil?

options.A: Topical antibiotics
options.B: Organic nitrates
options.C: Oral multivitamins
options.D: Antihistamines

explanation: Safety first! Mixing ED meds with nitrates can cause a massive, dangerous crash in blood pressure. Never combine them!

question: Clearing out stagnant water pools around houses is mainly done to control which element of disease spread?

options.A: Reservoirs
options.B: Vectors
options.C: Direct contact
options.D: Airborne droplets

explanation: You're doing great! Standing water is a breeding ground for mosquitoes, which act as vectors carrying diseases like malaria to us.

question: Why are traditional media like local drama and folk songs so effective in rural health education?

options.A: They replace the need for community health nurses entirely
options.B: They cost nothing to produce compared to printing posters and books
options.C: They are scientifically proven to kill infectious bacteria instantly
options.D: They are culturally familiar, entertaining, and work well even with low literacy

explanation: Music and drama speak straight to people's hearts and culture, making them brilliant tools even when community members can't read well.

question: What is the term for long-term liver damage caused by repeated inflammation and severe scarring?

options.A: Cholelithiasis
options.B: Steatosis
options.C: Cirrhosis
options.D: Necrosis

explanation: You're doing great! Over time, constant scarring replaces healthy liver tissue with tough fibrous tissue. We call this condition cirrhosis.

question: What percentage of pre-pregnancy weight loss is typically used to help define hyperemesis gravidarum?

options.A: Exactly 10%
options.B: Greater than 5%
options.C: Less than 1%
options.D: Around 20%

explanation: Losing more than 5 percent of pre-pregnancy body weight due to continuous vomiting points strongly toward hyperemesis gravidarum. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h2)

question: When a mosquito bites you and passes on the malaria parasite, what kind of transmission is this?

options.A: Contact transmission
options.B: Vehicle-borne transmission
options.C: Vector-borne transmission
options.D: Droplet transmission

explanation: Vectors are living creatures, like mosquitoes or ticks, that carry germs from one person or animal to another. Great clinical connection for Nigerian nursing practice!

question: What is a common challenge hospitals face regarding waste management in resource-limited settings?

options.A: A complete absence of patients generating any hazardous waste
options.B: An overwhelming surplus of high-tech microwave sterilization units
options.C: Excessive funding that leads to over-purchasing of medical bins
options.D: Erratic power supply and scarcity of specialized color-coded bags

explanation: Spot on! Power cuts and shortages of proper bags make safe waste sorting a real challenge in many local facilities. Keep up the good work!

question: What does non-exercise activity thermogenesis (NEAT) mean in daily life?

options.A: Energy used only during scheduled gym workouts
options.B: Calories burned through everyday movements like walking and fidgeting
options.C: Resting calories used by the heart while sleeping
options.D: Heat generated by a fever during an infection

explanation: NEAT is a fancy term for a simple idea: it's all the calories you burn just moving around during your normal day, outside of going to the gym!

question: What do we call the type of laryngoscopy that uses a thin, flexible camera passed through the nose?

options.A: Indirect mirror laryngoscopy
options.B: Open surgical laryngoscopy
options.C: Rigid direct laryngoscopy
options.D: Fiberoptic laryngoscopy

explanation: You got it! A fiberoptic scope uses a flexible, thin camera that slides easily through the nose while the patient is awake.

question: What is a major practical challenge to good clinical supervision in busy Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: An excess of well-trained administrative supervisors
options.B: Complete absence of any clinical policies or guidelines
options.C: Heavy staff workloads and severe staff shortages
options.D: Too much free time available during morning shifts

explanation: We all know how packed the wards can get! High patient numbers and few staff members make it tough to find time for mentoring.

question: What is the most important piece of advice to give a patient who has recovered from serum sickness before they leave the hospital?

options.A: Demonstrate how to measure blood pressure at home twice daily
options.B: Encourage the patient to eat a high-protein diet to rebuild lost muscle
options.C: Instruct the patient to exercise their joints vigorously every single morning
options.D: Teach the patient to permanently avoid the specific triggering drug

explanation: Prevention is key! They must avoid that specific drug forever, because taking it again can cause an even faster and worse reaction.

question: A client gets mild sedation to stay calm during a long MRI. What must the nurse watch most closely?

options.A: Breathing rate and oxygen levels
options.B: Bowel sounds in all four abdominal areas
options.C: The exact room temperature
options.D: How fast the client can walk afterward

explanation: Sedatives can slow down breathing, so keeping an eye on the patient's respiratory rate and oxygen is top priority!

question: How does social justice guide a community health nurse during advocacy?

options.A: It drives the nurse to fight for fair access to health resources for everyone
options.B: It requires the nurse to obey hospital management without question
options.C: It forces the nurse to prioritize wealthy patients who pay higher taxes
options.D: It allows the nurse to make medical diagnoses independently

explanation: Well done! Social justice is about fairness—making sure everyone, rich or poor, gets a fair share of healthcare resources to close health gaps.

question: What does 'medicalisation of FGM' actually mean?

options.A: Using modern anesthesia during traditional cutting
options.B: Researching new surgical methods to reverse FGM
options.C: Treating the medical complications caused by FGM
options.D: FGM procedures being performed by healthcare workers

explanation: Medicalisation simply means when doctors, nurses, or other health workers are the ones performing the cutting. It's dangerous because it wrongly makes the practice look safe or acceptable.

question: What is the main difference between bacterial and viral STIs in the body?

options.A: Bacterial infections cause permanent cellular mutations, while viral infections do not
options.B: Viral infections remain in the body long-term, while bacterial infections are usually cured
options.C: Viral infections never respond to any form of pharmaceutical treatment
options.D: Bacterial infections require lifelong maintenance therapy instead of short courses

explanation: Spot on! Bacteria can usually be kicked out with medications, but viruses like HIV or herpes stay in the body for life and need long-term management.

question: Who chooses the Village Health Workers to serve in rural communities?

options.A: The federal minister of health
options.B: The community members themselves
options.C: International donor agencies
options.D: Private pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Wonderful! When the community picks their own health worker, it builds instant trust and ensures the care fits their local culture.

question: What is the primary role of the nurse when patients want to use complementary or alternative therapies?

options.A: Forbidding patients from using any therapy not written in the doctor's orders
options.B: Personally performing massage and aromatherapy for every single patient
options.C: Ensuring safe use, providing education, and supporting patient preferences
options.D: Selling herbal supplements to patients to help fund the hospital ward

explanation: Well done! Nurses act as educators and safety advocates, helping patients safely blend alternative methods with their standard medical care.

question: Why is stomach pumping (gastric lavage) rarely done if a patient seeks help hours after swallowing a poison?

options.A: Gastric lavage only works on poisons that were inhaled
options.B: The poison has already passed from the stomach into the small intestines
options.C: Activated charcoal neutralizes the need for any washing
options.D: The stomach lining becomes too tough for tubes to pass safely

explanation: Makes total sense, right? If hours have passed, the poison has already moved past the stomach, making pumping ineffective.

question: Which nursing action is an example of secondary prevention for a blood disorder?

options.A: Educating the community about eating iron-rich foods
options.B: Screening routine complete blood counts for a pregnant woman
options.C: Administering a blood transfusion for severe hemorrhagic shock
options.D: Providing physical therapy for joint damage in hemophilia

explanation: Secondary prevention involves early detection and screening to catch conditions before they cause severe problems. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h1)

question: What symptom makes vitamin B12 deficiency different from simple iron deficiency?

options.A: Elevation in total white blood cell counts
options.B: Severe swelling in the lower extremities
options.C: Presence of neurological symptoms like numbness
options.D: Rapid drop in liver enzyme production

explanation: B12 protects our nerves! When it's missing, patients can experience tingling or numbness in their hands and feet, which doesn't happen in plain iron deficiency.

question: What does a quantitative research design primarily rely on?

options.A: Long personal diaries and emotional stories
options.B: Historical paintings and cultural myths
options.C: Numerical data and statistical analysis
options.D: Unstructured casual conversations

explanation: Quantitative studies focus on measurements, counts, and statistical tests to evaluate variables. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T1#GNS217_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which of these activities is a core part of the global definition of nursing?

options.A: Filing hospital tax returns and insurance claims
options.B: Promoting healthy lifestyles in local communities
options.C: Purchasing pharmaceutical drugs for wholesale markets
options.D: Designing architectural layouts for new surgical suites

explanation: Nursing goes beyond treating sick people in wards; we also actively promote health and prevent illness right inside our communities! [learn more](GNS112_U1_T1#GNS112_U1_T1_h3)

question: When does everyday worry cross the line into a clinical anxiety disorder?

options.A: Normal worry only occurs in children and teenagers.
options.B: Normal worry never causes physical symptoms like a racing heart.
options.C: Clinical anxiety persists excessively and disrupts daily functioning.
options.D: Clinical anxiety disappears immediately once a stressor is removed.

explanation: We all worry about exams or finances sometimes! But clinical anxiety hangs around stubbornly and makes it hard to get through daily life. Spotting this difference helps you understand when a patient truly needs support.

question: As a student nurse, how often should you check and inspect an active peripheral IV site on your patient?

options.A: Once every 48 hours during dressing changes
options.B: Only when the patient complains of severe pain
options.C: Only when the infusion bag runs completely empty
options.D: At least once every nursing shift

explanation: Exactly! Regular checks each shift help you catch tiny problems like early swelling or soreness before they turn into bigger issues.

question: What happens to the spread of disease if a nurse successfully breaks even one link in the chain of infection?

options.A: The pathogen automatically changes into a harmless bacteria
options.B: The patient develops instant immunity against all other germs
options.C: The infection cycle is stopped and disease spread is prevented
options.D: The reservoir completely disappears from the environment

explanation: Because the chain requires every single link to function, breaking just one link halts the entire transmission process. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is a parallax error when reading a scale, and how do you prevent it?

options.A: An error caused by the patient wearing heavy rubber shoes
options.B: An inaccurate reading caused by looking at the scale from an angle instead of straight at eye level
options.C: A mechanical failure caused by sliding the heavy counterweight too fast
options.D: A false measurement resulting from an unlevel floor surface

explanation: Looking at a scale from above or below skews the numbers. Always read the measurement directly at eye level to get it right!

question: Which of the following is classified as a macromineral?

options.A: Iron
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Zinc
options.D: Iodine

explanation: Calcium is a macromineral because the body requires it in large amounts daily, primarily for bone health and muscle function. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T9#GNS215_U6_T9_h3)

question: A patient with hypertension is discharged from a federal teaching hospital. What should the local community health nurse do next?

options.A: Wait for the patient to develop a stroke before taking any action
options.B: Tell the patient never to visit the teaching hospital again for any reason
options.C: Monitor blood pressure regularly and check that prescribed drugs are taken correctly
options.D: Throw away the hospital discharge summary and start a new treatment plan

explanation: The nurse ensures continuity of care by supervising medication adherence and monitoring blood pressure at the local level. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T16#GNS225_U3_T16_h8)

question: Why does Primary Health Care place such a strong focus on community participation?

options.A: Because nurses are not trained to administer vaccines without civilian supervision
options.B: Because the government lacks any funding to pay healthcare workers
options.C: Because international laws forbid centralized hospital construction
options.D: Because programs are more successful and sustainable when locals help plan them

explanation: Exactly! When the community is involved from the start, health projects address real local needs and are warmly accepted.

question: What is the specific name for Cushing's syndrome when it is caused by a tiny tumor in the pituitary gland making too much ACTH?

options.A: Cushing's disease
options.B: Conn's syndrome
options.C: Pheochromocytoma
options.D: Addison's disease

explanation: Here is a handy clinical tip: 'Cushing's syndrome' is any excess cortisol, but when the pituitary gland's tumor is the culprit, we specifically call it 'Cushing's disease'.

question: A child with cerebral palsy presents with very stiff muscles and hyperactive reflexes. Which type of cerebral palsy is this child most likely experiencing?

options.A: Ataxic
options.B: Dyskinetic
options.C: Flaccid
options.D: Spastic

explanation: Spastic cerebral palsy is marked by increased muscle tone and exaggerated reflexes because of injury to the motor cortex or pyramidal tracts. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h3)

question: Which type of ovarian cyst can contain unusual tissues like hair or teeth?

options.A: Follicular cyst
options.B: Dermoid cyst
options.C: Endometrioma
options.D: Corpus luteum cyst

explanation: Dermoid cysts sound a bit wild, but they just develop from germ cells and can sometimes contain quirky tissues like skin, hair, or teeth!

question: What is the key difference between Acute Stress Disorder and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder?

options.A: Whether the patient has physical injuries or not
options.B: The time frame and duration of the symptoms
options.C: The age of the person experiencing the trauma
options.D: The specific type of disaster that caused the trauma

explanation: Acute Stress Disorder happens shortly after the event, whereas PTSD involves long-lasting symptoms that persist over months or years. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h3)

question: Which mental health condition is frequently missed in older adults because it often hides behind physical complaints like body aches?

options.A: Acute delirium
options.B: Bipolar mania
options.C: Depression
options.D: Schizophrenia

explanation: Good to know! Depression in seniors is easy to miss because they might talk about constant tiredness or aches instead of feeling sad.

question: A patient with a new leg cast says their toes feel very numb and tingly. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Perform a complete neurovascular assessment and report findings
options.B: Massage the toes gently to restore normal local blood circulation
options.C: Elevate the leg above heart level and encourage deep breathing
options.D: Administer a prescribed oral sleeping pill to calm the patient

explanation: Numbness and tingling are red flags for trapped nerves or poor blood flow. Checking thoroughly and reporting right away keeps the patient safe.

question: When putting in a diaphragm correctly, where should the front edge be tucked?

options.A: Against the anterior vaginal wall
options.B: Behind the pubic bone
options.C: Directly over the labia majora
options.D: Inside the uterine cavity

explanation: The front rim needs to hook securely behind the pubic bone so it stays locked tightly over the cervix.

question: What size syringe should you use when trying to clear a blocked nasogastric tube?

options.A: 3 mL standard syringe
options.B: 1 mL insulin syringe
options.C: 5 mL tuberculin syringe
options.D: 30 mL or larger syringe

explanation: Always grab a 30 mL or bigger syringe! Small syringes build up too much pressure and can burst the plastic tubing, whereas bigger syringes spread out the force safely.

question: What is the primary goal of the teach-back method during patient education?

options.A: To test the patient's ability to read complex medical textbooks
options.B: To prove that the nurse is an expert in pharmacology
options.C: To check if the patient truly understands their medication instructions
options.D: To make the nursing consultation take longer than necessary

explanation: The teach-back method requires the client to repeat instructions in their own words, confirming comprehension and revealing any remaining confusion. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T2#GNS215_U4_T2_h5)

question: Why is asking about a patient's job so important during a health assessment?

options.A: It proves the employer is legally guilty of negligence
options.B: It determines the exact salary the worker earns each month
options.C: It replaces the need for standard physical examinations
options.D: It links patient symptoms to exposures in their workplace

explanation: Many illnesses build up slowly over time. Knowing what a patient does for a living helps us connect the dots to their health issues.

question: What is the most effective approach a nurse should take when providing nutritional counseling to a nursing mother?

options.A: Assess her current diet and suggest affordable, local food options
options.B: Demand that she buy expensive imported supplements and vitamins
options.C: Provide a rigid meal plan without asking about her cultural preferences
options.D: Assume she already knows everything because postpartum nutrition is instinctive

explanation: Good counseling respects the mother's financial and cultural reality by building on affordable, local food sources she already knows. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to health behavior change in primary care?

options.A: High rates of illiteracy among the target audience
options.B: Extreme poverty and lack of basic financial resources
options.C: Deep-seated cultural norms and traditional beliefs
options.D: Guaranteed financial wealth for every household

explanation: Poverty, illiteracy, and strong cultural traditions can make health changes tough, but having guaranteed wealth certainly wouldn't be a barrier! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h8)

question: What is the main goal of tertiary prevention when caring for patients with sensory loss?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any future medical checkups
options.B: To prevent healthy family members from developing the condition
options.C: To completely reverse the underlying genetic cause of the disease
options.D: To limit disability and maximize remaining functional independence

explanation: Tertiary prevention is all about rehabilitation and helping people live their best, most independent lives even after a permanent loss. You're doing great learning these levels of prevention!

question: Why must you document a medication immediately after giving it, rather than waiting until the end of your shift?

options.A: Because hospital computers automatically shut down at noon
options.B: To finish paperwork quickly so the nurse can take a break
options.C: To prevent another nurse from accidentally giving a second duplicate dose
options.D: To let the pharmacy know the pill bottle is now empty

explanation: Immediate charting lets the whole healthcare team know the job is done, keeping the patient safe from getting a accidental double dose later!

question: What do we call sketchy publishers that charge money to print articles quickly without doing real peer review?

options.A: Predatory journals
options.B: Grey literature
options.C: Primary sources
options.D: Systematic databases

explanation: You're doing great! Predatory journals take cash from authors just to publish fake or unvetted work—always watch out for them!

question: Why is communication evaluated right alongside clinical nursing skills?

options.A: Soft skills replace the need for formal nursing board examinations
options.B: Clinical skills are entirely separate from how a nurse talks to patients
options.C: Communication scores are the only data required by insurance companies
options.D: Nursing requires effective teamwork and clear handovers to keep patients safe

explanation: Even if you are great at procedures, nursing is a team sport. Clear handovers and warm patient communication are vital to prevent mistakes.

question: Which lethal heart rhythm requires immediate defibrillation and emergency response?

options.A: First-degree heart block
options.B: Sinus bradycardia
options.C: Premature atrial contractions
options.D: Ventricular fibrillation

explanation: Ventricular fibrillation is a chaotic heart rhythm where the ventricles quiver instead of pumping blood, causing cardiac arrest that requires immediate electrical shock. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h4)

question: Your patient has a radial arterial line, and suddenly their hand looks pale, feels cold, and has a weak pulse. What is your very first step?

options.A: Apply a warm heating pad directly over the plastic catheter hub
options.B: Inflate the blood pressure cuff on that exact arm to high pressure
options.C: Document the finding as a normal reaction and check again in four hours
options.D: Notify the healthcare provider right away and assess distal circulation

explanation: That's a red flag for poor blood flow past the line! Whenever a limb turns cold and pale, you must act fast and alert the doctor to protect the tissue.

question: Which of these activities counts toward Nigeria's GDP?

options.A: A Nigerian nurse working in a London hospital
options.B: A retired Nigerian citizen receiving a pension abroad
options.C: A foreign company manufacturing drugs entirely overseas
options.D: A foreign doctor treating patients at a private clinic in Lagos

explanation: You've got this! Because the medical service takes place physically inside Nigeria, it contributes to Nigeria's GDP.

question: What is the main purpose of using a problem tree analysis in community health?

options.A: To map out the geographical boundaries of a farming community
options.B: To measure the exact height and weight of growing children
options.C: To trace visible symptoms back to their underlying root causes
options.D: To calculate the total financial cost of buying medical drugs

explanation: A problem tree helps health workers look past surface symptoms to find the true core cause of a health issue. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h3)

question: Why is the psychological trauma of breast ironing often exceptionally severe for young girls?

options.A: It is openly discussed by the entire community every day
options.B: It is inflicted by trusted family members meant to protect them
options.C: It forces victims to drop out of school permanently
options.D: It causes immediate and total memory loss

explanation: When mothers or grandmothers commit the abuse, the child experiences a severe betrayal of trust. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h5)

question: What does reproductive health cover according to standard health definitions?

options.A: Only the ability to bear children without medical complications
options.B: The prevention of sexually transmitted diseases in teenagers
options.C: The total absence of any infection in the pelvic organs
options.D: Complete physical, mental, and social well-being in all reproductive matters

explanation: Reproductive health is a broad state of complete well-being, not merely the absence of disease or infirmity in reproductive organs. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h1)

question: Why must a patient wait nearly three months to check if lifestyle changes improved his sperm count?

options.A: It takes roughly two to three months for new sperm to fully develop and mature
options.B: Hormone medications prescribed by the doctor require ninety days to activate
options.C: The laboratory needs multiple samples collected over a twelve-week period
options.D: Sperm cells live inside the male reproductive tract for a maximum of ninety days

explanation: Since spermatogenesis takes about 64 to 74 days, any healthy lifestyle changes will take that long to show up in a fresh batch of mature sperm!

question: How do Electronic Health Records mainly improve teamwork among healthcare professionals?

options.A: By eliminating the need for nurses and doctors to ever speak to each other
options.B: By replacing all physical bedside shift handovers with text messages
options.C: By allowing instant access to updated patient notes across different departments
options.D: By automatically deciding the medical diagnosis for every admitted patient

explanation: Instant digital access means doctors, nurses, and pharmacists can see the same up-to-date information simultaneously, improving coordination of care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T1#GNS113_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the best feeding practice recommended for an infant's first six months of life?

options.A: Exclusive breastfeeding
options.B: Water and thin maize pap
options.C: Mashed family meals
options.D: Goat milk and infant formula

explanation: Correct! Breast milk alone provides all the water, nutrients, and antibodies a baby needs for the first six months. Nothing else is required! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h7)

question: When is it appropriate for a nurse to stop performing CPR?

options.A: When trained medical help arrives and takes over care
options.B: When family members ask the team to take a break
options.C: As soon as the nurse feels physically tired and sweaty
options.D: After five minutes of continuous compressions without a pulse

explanation: CPR continues until the patient recovers, professionals take over, or clear signs of death appear. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h8)

question: Which symptom along with tummy cramps in early pregnancy is a major red flag?

options.A: Mild morning nausea
options.B: Occasional breast tenderness
options.C: Vaginal bleeding
options.D: Increased skin pigmentation

explanation: Bleeding combined with cramps always needs quick medical attention because it can point to a potential miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy. You are learning to spot the crucial signs!

question: You see an elderly patient from a remote village showing muscle wasting and slow wound healing during the lean season. What should you suspect first?

options.A: Nutritional vulnerability caused by seasonal food availability limits
options.B: A rare genetic disorder affecting the patient's digestion
options.C: An acute allergic reaction to local agricultural crops
options.D: Excessive physical activity during the harvest period

explanation: The timing (lean season) and location (remote village) strongly point to a lack of seasonal food as the root cause of the malnutrition. Spot on!

question: Why is it sometimes good if a deworming drug stays in the gut and isn't easily absorbed into the blood?

options.A: It ensures the drug travels directly to the brain tissues
options.B: It prevents the liver from metabolizing any medication
options.C: It reduces the need for patients to drink water
options.D: It keeps the medication concentration high inside the gut lumen

explanation: Makes sense, right? Keeping the drug right in the intestines means it hits the tummy-dwelling worms with full force!

question: How can you make sure your patient truly understands a new reproductive medication?

options.A: By assuming the pharmacist already covered everything needed
options.B: By handing the patient a technical textbook to read alone
options.C: By focusing only on how much the prescription costs
options.D: By explaining expected benefits, side effects, and warning signs clearly

explanation: Exactly! Taking time to explain how the drug works and what side effects to watch for helps your patient stay safe and confident.

question: What is the main job of 'moulding' during labour?

options.A: To increase the total volume of brain tissue
options.B: To permanently fuse the cranial sutures early
options.C: To prevent the baby from breathing amniotic fluid
options.D: To reduce the skull dimensions to fit the pelvis

explanation: Moulding is the baby's superpower for birth! The skull bones gently overlap so the head shapes itself to fit easily through the birth canal without harming the brain.

question: Why do nurses auscultate (listen) before palpating (feeling) the abdomen?

options.A: To make the patient feel warmer
options.B: Because palpation takes too long to finish
options.C: To prevent the stethoscope from getting dirty
options.D: To avoid altering natural bowel sounds

explanation: If you press or rub the belly first (palpation), you wake up the intestines and create fake bowel sounds. Always listen first so you hear what's naturally going on!

question: Which laboratory sample is most commonly checked to confirm a lung fluke infection?

options.A: Cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: Sputum
options.C: Urine
options.D: Venous blood cultures

explanation: Correct! Looking at a sputum sample under a microscope to find the parasite's eggs is the standard way to confirm the diagnosis.

question: Which core nursing ethic requires you to keep a survivor's identity and story strictly secret?

options.A: Beneficence
options.B: Justice
options.C: Veracity
options.D: Confidentiality

explanation: Confidentiality protects patients from stigma and further danger by making sure their private health details never leak out without their consent.

question: What is the main focus of a physical therapist visiting a patient at home?

options.A: Providing emotional counseling for grief
options.B: Assisting with daily grocery shopping
options.C: Restoring physical mobility and strength
