explanation: Pus and redness are classic signs that white blood cells are fighting a heavy bacterial invasion in the tissue. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h7)

question: Why is it so important for nurses to offer non-judgmental counseling when discussing sexual health?

options.A: It legally waives the hospital from liability during invasive pelvic examinations
options.B: It builds trust, encouraging patients to share accurate health history and seek timely care
options.C: It guarantees that the patient will never contract a viral infection in the future
options.D: It eliminates the need for laboratory diagnostic testing during clinical visits

explanation: When patients feel judged or shamed, they hide their symptoms and avoid clinics. A warm, open approach keeps them safe and cared for!

question: Intimate partner violence (IPV) often starts quietly. Which behavior is a typical early warning sign?

options.A: Sudden financial ruin orchestrated by external family members
options.B: Unprovoked legal action regarding property ownership
options.C: Immediate and severe physical assaults in public places
options.D: Subtle emotional degradation and controlling behaviors

explanation: Well done! IPV rarely starts with physical blows; it usually creeps in through subtle control, insults, and isolation before turning physical. Always keep your eyes open for these red flags!

question: Which of these signs is the classic giveaway that an IV has 'infiltrated' (leaked into the tissue)?

options.A: A warm, red, hard streak running all the way up the arm
options.B: Severe chest pain accompanied by audible lung crackles
options.C: Bright red bleeding gushing out around the plastic catheter
options.D: Swelling, coolness, and pallor around the insertion site

explanation: Spot on! When IV fluid leaks into the tissue instead of the vein, it makes the skin look pale, feel cool, and swell up. Time to restart the line!

question: You walk into the clinic and notice a toddler with swollen feet (edema) and sparse, discolored hair. What is your best next nursing action?

options.A: Assume the child has an infectious tropical disease and isolate them
options.B: Scold the mother for failing to feed the child expensive foreign foods
options.C: Discharge the child immediately with a prescription for multivitamins
options.D: Assess for protein-energy malnutrition and inquire about local food taboos

explanation: Those classic signs point right to malnutrition. A good nurse investigates gently, checking if restrictive family food habits are playing a role.

question: At what point during your shift should you separate (segregate) hospital waste?

options.A: Right at the exact time and place you create it
options.B: After the cleaning staff pack the bins
options.C: When the waste reaches the hospital incinerator
options.D: During weekly environmental health inspections

explanation: Always sort your waste immediately as you generate it! Waiting until later leads to mistakes and accidental injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T2#GNS122_U5_T2_h7)

question: A newly opened nursing home focuses entirely on packing in as many residents as possible to maximize government payouts. Based on trends from the 1960s and 70s, what is a likely result?

options.A: Excessive funding directly spent on recreational programs
options.B: Compromised quality of resident care and severe staff burnout
options.C: Immediate elimination of all chronic health conditions
options.D: Universal praise from visiting public health inspectors

explanation: When a facility chases high numbers over quality care, they usually cut corners on staffing. This leaves nurses overworked and patients getting less-than-ideal attention.

question: What is a key action public health nurses take to improve community nutrition?

options.A: Growing all the crops needed for the entire country inside hospitals
options.B: Organizing nutritional screenings and educating families on budget-friendly local meals
options.C: Passing strict laws to ban all processed foods globally
options.D: Taking over the management of international cargo shipping lines

explanation: Spot on! Nurses play a huge role by checking nutritional status and teaching families how to cook healthy, pocket-friendly local meals.

question: Why can autonomic nerve failure cause a patient to feel dizzy when standing up?

options.A: The inner ear fills with fluid from poor circulation
options.B: Blood pressure drops drastically because vessels fail to constrict
options.C: Eye muscles become too weak to focus on light
options.D: Brain cells instantly run out of oxygen and die

explanation: Normally, your nerves quickly tighten your blood vessels when you stand up to keep blood flowing to your head. When those nerves fail, blood pressure drops and you feel dizzy.

question: What is the primary purpose of the nasal conchae or turbinates on the lateral wall?

options.A: To trap large dust particles directly at the external nares
options.B: To produce tears that lubricate the nasal mucosa
options.C: To create turbulent airflow and increase surface area
options.D: To house the specialized receptors for the sense of taste

explanation: The curvy shape of the conchae forces air to swirl around, maximizing contact with the warm, moist lining so it gets conditioned properly. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h2)

question: Which group of professionals is most ideal for creating a complete care plan for a special needs child?

options.A: Only traditional spiritual healers
options.B: A multidisciplinary team including nurses, therapists, and social workers
options.C: Only hospital accountants and security guards
options.D: Exclusive teams of pharmaceutical sales reps

explanation: Special needs touch on health, education, and social life, so working together in a multidisciplinary team gives the child the best possible holistic care.

question: How should an airport security check be handled for a passenger with a pacemaker?

options.A: Turn off the pacemaker completely using an external switch before entering the security line
options.B: Walk through the metal detector normally, but ask security to avoid using a hand-held wand over the chest
options.C: Show the medical card and demand a full body cavity search instead of walking through arches
options.D: Refuse all security screening because airport machines will instantly destroy the pacemaker

explanation: Walking through the security arch is usually fine if you keep moving, but security should avoid holding a magnetic wand directly over the chest. Practical knowledge for clinical practice!

question: Why is it so vital for a nurse to keep a non-judgmental attitude during sexual health assessments?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing barrier methods
options.B: It encourages the patient to share accurate health history and seek care
options.C: It eliminates the need for laboratory diagnostic testing
options.D: It guarantees the patient will never contract another infection

explanation: Spot on! When patients feel safe and respected without shame, they are honest about their health and more likely to get help.

question: As a nurse, what is a key responsibility when positioning a patient for an operation?

options.A: Leaving all joints uncovered so they can move freely during prep
options.B: Padding bony prominences to prevent pressure sores and nerve injury
options.C: Tying the patient tightly to the operating table with heavy restraints
options.D: Ensuring the patient's head hangs lower than the body at all times

explanation: Patients lie still for a long time under anesthesia, so careful padding protects their joints, skin, and nerves from damage.

question: Why is Directly Observed Therapy (DOT) used for treating patients with tuberculosis?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of hospital building construction
options.B: To punish patients who forget to visit the clinic on time
options.C: To ensure patients take every dose correctly and prevent drug resistance
options.D: To make the tuberculosis bacteria grow faster in the lungs

explanation: Watching patients take their medication guarantees adherence, which stops dangerous drug-resistant strains of tuberculosis from emerging. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T4#GNS124_U1_T4_h7)

question: Why are supportive national policies so important for keeping reproductive health services running?

options.A: They secure long-term government funding and legal protection for healthcare programs
options.B: They allow individual hospitals to ignore international health standards
options.C: They prevent community members from asking questions about medical care
options.D: They ensure that healthcare providers never have to undergo professional training

explanation: National policies give healthcare programs the legal backing and steady funds they need to survive even when government leaders change. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T2#GNS312_U5_T2_h8)

question: Why is advance care planning so important for older adults?

options.A: It guarantees that residents will never experience physical pain
options.B: It ensures the resident's personal wishes for end-of-life care are known and honored
options.C: It prevents nurses from having to communicate with grieving relatives
options.D: It legally forces family members to pay for expensive surgeries

explanation: Talking about preferences early on ensures that future medical decisions truly reflect what the resident wants when they can no longer speak for themselves.

question: A patient comes back three days after an injection with a hot, swollen, throbbing lump at the site. What is this most likely?

options.A: A localized muscle abscess
options.B: Systemic blood poisoning
options.C: Chronic hepatitis C infection
options.D: An acute HIV seroconversion illness

explanation: That classic combo of throbbing pain, heat, swelling, and a lump usually points to a bacterial abscess from an unsterile injection that may need draining.

question: Which reflex is NOT coordinated by the medulla oblongata?

options.A: The swallowing reflex
options.B: The coughing reflex
options.C: The vomiting reflex
options.D: Visual tracking of a moving object

explanation: Visual tracking is handled by higher brain areas and midbrain structures, whereas vomiting, swallowing, and coughing are medullary reflexes. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h5)

question: What is the primary age threshold that defines early marriage globally?

options.A: Under 21 years
options.B: Under 16 years
options.C: Under 18 years
options.D: Under 15 years

explanation: Global public health and human rights frameworks classify any marriage involving a person under 18 years as an early or child marriage. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h1)

question: What makes droplet nuclei so tricky when it comes to spreading infections?

options.A: Blocking the entry of viruses into the upper respiratory tract
options.B: Causing localized skin infections through direct contact
options.C: Settling immediately on nearby surfaces within one meter
options.D: Carrying airborne infectious pathogens over long distances

explanation: Great job thinking about how germs travel! Droplet nuclei are tiny dried-out particles that stay floating in the air for a long time, letting them travel far on air currents.

question: What does the abbreviation SBAR stand for in clinical communication?

options.A: Safety, Briefing, Assessment, Review
options.B: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation
options.C: Symptoms, Blood pressure, Activity, Rate
options.D: System, Bedside, Action, Record

explanation: You got it! SBAR is your trusty tool for sharing clear, snappy patient updates with doctors and fellow nurses.

question: Why should you regularly check the status indicator light on an AED machine?

options.A: To calibrate the internal thermometer for accurate skin readings
options.B: To measure how many shocks are left in the main computer processor
options.C: To ensure the voice volume is loud enough for a noisy room
options.D: To confirm that the internal battery and system components are operational

explanation: Routine checks make sure the machine is ready to work the exact second an emergency happens. Good nursing practice!

question: What is a major benefit of community genetic counseling for inherited blood disorders?

options.A: Manufacturing safe blood products for local hospital use
options.B: Providing free meals for patients with severe chronic anemia
options.C: Helping families understand their risk of passing conditions to children
options.D: Treating acute bleeding episodes in emergency rooms

explanation: Genetic counseling educates couples about their carrier status and the statistical chances of having children with conditions like sickle cell anemia. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h7)

question: What is the main goal of the intensive phase of TB treatment?

options.A: To test if the patient is allergic to all four drugs
options.B: To rapidly reduce the bacterial load and stop infectiousness
options.C: To rebuild the damaged lung tissue back to normal
options.D: To completely finish the entire course of treatment

explanation: Hitting TB hard with four drugs quickly drops the germ count so the patient stops spreading it to others. Excellent clinical milestone!

question: Why is it better to call for an emergency medical assistance team early instead of waiting for a full cardiac arrest?

options.A: It reduces the cost of hospital medications.
options.B: It keeps the hospital hallways quiet during visiting hours.
options.C: It prevents doctors from having to do paperwork later.
options.D: It allows the team to treat the underlying cause before the heart stops.

explanation: Once a patient's heart stops, their chance of surviving intact drops significantly compared to catching and fixing the problem while they still have a pulse. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the best nursing advice for a mum with painful, engorged breasts?

options.A: Instructing her to stop all fluid intake for the next three days
options.B: Advising her to wait twelve hours between feeds to rest the tissue
options.C: Applying ice packs to completely block the prolactin hormone
options.D: Encouraging frequent milk removal through nursing or expressing

explanation: Well done! Getting the milk out relieves the pressure, eases the pain, and keeps milk flowing nicely for the baby.

question: If someone accidentally gets a corrosive chemical in their eyes or on their skin, what is the recommended minimum time to flush it with clean water?

options.A: Exactly 30 seconds
options.B: At least 15 minutes
options.C: Until the burning stops
options.D: One full hour

explanation: You nailed it! Flushing continuously for at least 15 minutes is crucial to dilute the chemical and wash it away before it burns deep into the tissue.

question: Why are infants and young children considered a nutritionally vulnerable group?

options.A: Their rapid growth and development require lots of nutrients
options.B: Their bodies do not require protein during early childhood
options.C: They possess fully developed immune systems that reject food
options.D: They refuse to eat any form of solid food until age five

explanation: Kids grow so fast! If their diet falls short even a little bit, it can quickly lead to poor growth or malnutrition.

question: What does a demographic rate typically measure?

options.A: The weight of medical equipment in a ward
options.B: The physical size of a community health center
options.C: The exact total money spent on healthcare
options.D: How often an event happens in a population over time

explanation: Rates show the frequency of specific occurrences, like births or deaths, relative to the total population size over a given period. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h3)

question: Why is clear, objective nursing documentation so crucial in skilled care facilities?

options.A: It is only used by insurance companies to deny resident coverage.
options.B: It guarantees that no resident will ever experience a fall.
options.C: It serves as a legal safeguard and proves that skilled criteria were met.
options.D: It replaces the need for verbal shift handovers between nurses.

explanation: Good charting is your best friend! It acts as a legal proof that the resident truly needed and received expert nursing care.

question: What is the main job of the motor areas in the brain's cerebral cortex?

options.A: Interpreting sounds and spoken language
options.B: Storing long-term episodic memories
options.C: Controlling voluntary muscle movements
options.D: Processing visual images from the eyes

explanation: You've got this! The motor areas are specially designed to plan and make happen all the voluntary movements your body makes every day.

question: What is the main difference between nursing malpractice and ordinary negligence?

options.A: Malpractice only happens when a patient dies in the ICU
options.B: Ordinary negligence can only be committed by doctors
options.C: Malpractice involves specialized professional skills and breaches of professional standards
options.D: Ordinary negligence carries heavier criminal prison sentences in Nigeria

explanation: You got it! Malpractice specifically applies when a licensed professional's specialized care falls below their training standards.

question: Why did older medical books divide these drugs into major and minor tranquilizers?

options.A: Depending on whether the patient is male or female
options.B: Based on how strong the drug is and how serious the condition is
options.C: According to the physical weight of the drug tablet
options.D: To separate drugs made from plants from lab-made ones

explanation: Think of major tranquilizers as handling severe mental disturbances, while minor ones manage milder anxiety. Simple and clear!

question: What is one of the best bathroom upgrades to help prevent nasty falls?

options.A: Waxing the bathroom floor for easy cleaning
options.B: Installing sturdy grab bars near the toilet and shower
options.C: Using low-wattage bulbs for a softer night light
options.D: Placing decorative throw rugs on slippery tiles

explanation: Correct! Wet tiles are extremely slippery, and having firm grab bars to hold onto gives older adults the extra support they need.

question: What common tummy trouble can happen when a patient starts drinking full fluids that contain dairy?

options.A: Abdominal cramping and bloating
options.B: Rapid increase in bone density
options.C: High fever and skin rash
options.D: Sudden severe hair loss

explanation: Milk products can be a bit heavy on a recovering digestive system, sometimes causing temporary gas or cramps.

question: Your rural clinic keeps losing vaccines because of erratic power supply. What is the best immediate response that uses local community resources?

options.A: Wait for the federal government to rebuild the entire national electrical grid
options.B: Partner with local market leaders to mobilize a solar backup or reliable cold box system
options.C: Close the clinic permanently and refer all children to hospitals in the capital city
options.D: Blame the local residents for failing to generate their own electricity

explanation: Brilliant problem-solving! Instead of waiting for distant solutions, tapping into local networks and leaders helps you find practical, community-driven fixes right away.

question: What is the very first thing emergency responders do at an accident scene to protect a patient's spine?

options.A: Administering strong intravenous pain medication
options.B: Standing the patient up to test leg strength
options.C: Applying a rigid neck collar and securing the body
options.D: Massaging the neck muscles to relieve tension

explanation: That's correct! Putting on a stiff neck collar and securing the body keeps the spine still, preventing small fractures from turning into permanent paralysis.

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to changing health behaviors in a community?

options.A: Deeply rooted cultural myths and traditional practices
options.B: Language differences and lack of health literacy
options.C: Immediate access to fully stocked, free community pharmacies
options.D: Severe poverty making healthy choices unaffordable

explanation: You got it! Having easy access to free medical supplies actually helps people practice healthy habits rather than blocking them.

question: Which of the following is NOT a harmful traditional practice affecting reproductive health?

options.A: Female genital mutilation
options.B: Exclusive breastfeeding for infants
options.C: Taboos against sex education
options.D: Child marriage

explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding is a globally recommended health practice, unlike mutilation or child marriage which cause harm. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T6#GNS216_U1_T6_h4)
